data.content_ref: inline:The claim that large services are more resilient due to efficient 'circuit breaking' (SRC_001) contradicts the 'Redundancy Paradox' (SRC_002), as the latter posits that the very coordination layer required for such global management becomes the primary single point of failure. This relation is refuted if a coordination layer can be implemented that provides global load shedding without introducing a systemic single point of failure.
